name: Saint Raymond of Penyafort
history: A Catalan priest and canon lawyer who became a Dominican in middle age. Pope Gregory IX had him gather the Church’s scattered laws into a single collection, the Decretals, which remained at the heart of canon law for nearly seven centuries. Elected master of the Dominicans, he resigned after two years and went home to Barcelona to preach, hear confessions and work among Muslims and Jews.
life: Raymond taught law at Bologna before returning to Barcelona, where he joined the young Order of Preachers in 1222. He wrote a handbook for confessors that guided priests for generations. Called to Rome as chaplain and confessor to Gregory IX, he compiled the Decretals, published in 1234. In 1238 the Dominicans elected him their master general; he revised their constitutions and, in his sixties, resigned. Back in Catalonia he encouraged schools of Arabic and Hebrew so that friars could speak with Muslims and Jews in their own tongues, and tradition holds that he urged Saint Thomas Aquinas to write the Summa contra Gentiles. He is also remembered for helping Saint Peter Nolasco found the Mercedarians, who ransomed Christian captives. A well-loved legend says that when the king of Aragon refused him passage home from Majorca, he spread his cloak on the sea and sailed on it to Barcelona. He died there, nearly a hundred years old.
prayerTo: Saint Raymond, servant of justice and of mercy, you gave your learning to the Church and your old age to the poor and the sinner. Pray for lawyers, judges and confessors, that they may serve the truth with charity. Pray for me, that I may make a good confession and walk in the freedom of the children of God. Amen.
penance: Raymond guided confessors for centuries. Make a careful examination of conscience tonight and decide when you will next go to confession.
meditation: He was a master of law who knew that every law of the Church exists for the salvation of souls. Where do you keep the rules but forget their purpose?
